summary: AST is found in the liver but also in heart and skeletal muscle, so it is less liver-specific than ALT. Its main value is the ratio to ALT, which points towards different causes.
what_it_measures: The activity of aspartate aminotransferase in blood, reported in U/L.

interpretations.meaning: A raised AST can come from the liver or from muscle. An AST that is roughly twice the ALT is the classic pattern in alcohol-related liver disease; an isolated AST rise with normal ALT points at muscle instead.
typical_next_steps: creatine kinase if muscle is suspected

when_to_seek_help: AST is interpreted alongside ALT rather than alone. Discuss the pattern of your whole liver panel with your GP.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
